utility.notes: The Town's Resident Resources page lists Salt River Project (SRP) under Electricity, with the phone number 602-236-8888, in its list of helpful numbers for getting settled into a Queen Creek home. The Town's pages do not say that SRP serves every address in Queen Creek, and no other electric utility is named. To check your own address, use the address lookup on SRP's service area page, which shows the SRP services available at your location, and confirm the utility named on your electric bill.

generation_supplier.notes: The Town's pages do not name a separate generation supplier.

county.notes: The Town's sales tax page gives rate examples for a business operating in Queen Creek and Maricopa County and for one operating in Queen Creek and Pinal County.

permit_authority.value: Town of Queen Creek Building Safety Division
permit_authority.notes: The Building Safety division administers the Town's adopted building, plumbing, mechanical and electrical codes. The Town checks code compliance through plan review, permit issuance and inspection. A permit application and plans must be submitted to the Town before any construction project begins. Development Services is in the Municipal Services Building at 22358 S. Ellsworth Road, Queen Creek, AZ 85142, open 7 a.m. to 6 p.m. Monday through Thursday and closed on Fridays. A Queen Creek postal address might not mean the property is inside the Town's incorporated boundaries, which are separate from the 85142 and 85143 ZIP codes. The Town's pages do not say which office issues permits for a property outside its boundaries, so confirm your jurisdiction with the Town before you apply.

permit_url.notes: This is the Town's Solar Energy Systems page, which lists the solar permit fees and the engineer's report rules. Applications can be submitted online in the Development Nexus portal, where all Development Services functions are available. You need a registered account to submit an online application. Permit payments are only accepted through the Development Nexus portal, and the Town says legitimate payment emails come only from DevSvcsNexus@queencreekaz.gov.

interconnection_url.notes: This is SRP's residential distributed energy resource process checklist, and it applies if SRP is your electric utility. SRP's first step is to apply online through PowerClerk. SRP gives the customer six months to complete the Interconnection Agreement, installation and commissioning. SRP says systems should never be energized and operational before its official Final Inspection, when new meters are set, except for testing. SRP's program requires the system to be installed in SRP's electric service territory.

value.name: SRP Battery Partner
value.description: SRP says you can join and earn $55 per average kilowatt in incentives twice a year. Incentives are based on variables such as system storage size, customer load and system settings, and are paid as bill credits at the end of the summer and winter seasons. Enrolled batteries are selected for discharge during conservation events, and SRP says it will never discharge a battery below 20%. SRP describes it as a pilot approved for five years, ending April 30, 2030, and available to a maximum of 5,000 customers.
value.eligibility: For SRP customers with a battery from a participating battery partner: Enphase, Flip, FranklinWH, Tesla or Solar Edge. Check that SRP is your electric utility first.

battery_programs.notes: The Town describes no Town battery program. Its solar page does not address battery storage; its fee schedule lists a $200 Fire Prevention construction permit fee for Battery Systems but does not say whether it applies to a home battery, so ask Building Safety.

value.name: Online permit application in Development Nexus
value.required_when: Every project. A permit application and plans must be submitted before construction begins. The online application asks for the project description, project location, applicant contact information and an electronic signature or certification.

value.name: Plans with site plan and calculations, as one complete PDF file
value.required_when: Solar projects are submitted as one complete file with the site plan and calculations. Follow the Town's file formatting requirements for electronic submittals, and do not attach the paper application as a page inside the PDF.

value.name: Engineer's report for the supporting structure (when one of the Town's three criteria applies)
value.required_when: Required if the photovoltaic system's distributed weight is greater than 5 pounds per square foot, if it exerts a point load greater than 40 pounds, or if the home is more than 35 years old.

required_documents.notes: The Town says the majority of solar energy systems can be permitted without an engineer's report. The Town's Building Applications page lists a Contractor Declaration supplemental form and a Racking Configuration plan review checklist but does not say when they apply to a solar permit, so ask Building Safety.

value: Submit the permit application and plans online in Development Nexus.
The Town reviews the application and documents for completeness, then routes the plans for review.
The Town issues the permit after the plans are reviewed and approved.
If SRP is your utility, the application to SRP is made online through PowerClerk.
An SRP design consultant reviews the design diagrams, and SRP sends the property owner an Interconnection Agreement to sign.
SRP says the installer may install the system after SRP's design approval and all applicable building permits are in hand.
Schedule the Town inspections by phone at 480-358-3030, by text at 844-347-6270, or in Development Nexus.
After the system passes inspection, SRP's process calls for the jurisdiction to send SRP a City Clearance showing the system passed.
SRP performs its Final Inspection and installs new SRP meters.
SRP then issues a Permission to Operate letter to the installer and the customer.
inspection_steps.notes: The single family solar PV permit fee includes two inspections. The cutoff for next-business-day inspections is 6:00 p.m. The job card and the field set of plans must be on site for each inspection. The Town's inspections page says to use its inspection codes when requesting an inspection but does not list which codes apply to a solar permit, so ask Building Safety when you schedule. The Town permit, the Town inspections and SRP's Permission to Operate are separate approvals.

timeline_days.notes: The Town's solar page, fee schedule and Development Nexus pages give no review time for residential solar permits.

value.program_or_pathway: Single family residential solar PV permit (flat fee), applied for in Development Nexus
other_conditions: The Town uses three criteria to decide when an engineer's report for the supporting structure is necessary: the system weighs more than 5 pounds per square foot, exerts a point load over 40 pounds, or the home is more than 35 years old.
The Town adopted the 2021 International codes with an effective date of January 1, 2023, and its code list includes the 2020 National Electrical Code.

SRP interconnection rule (not a Town permit rule): the installation contractor must hold an Arizona R-11, CR-11 or R-39 (HVAC with solar only) license, and customers who self-install must comply with A.R.S. 32-1121.A.14.
The Town's pages do not say who may apply for a solar permit or whether an owner-builder may do the work, so ask Building Safety.
The Town's solar page does not address battery storage, ground-mounted systems, or adding to or replacing an existing system.

eligibility_constraints.notes: The licensing rule listed is SRP's, from its residential program requirements.

value.name: Single family residential solar photovoltaic system
value.unit: flat fee, includes one plan review and two inspections
value.notes: The Town's solar page and its fee schedule (item 25, Grid-Tied Photovoltaic System) both list $375. Nominal fees will be collected for complex or non-standard solar installations that need additional plan reviews or inspections.

value.name: Single family residential solar hot water heating system
value.notes: The Town's solar page says this fee includes one plan review and one inspection, while the fee schedule says it includes one plan review and two inspections, so confirm with Building Safety.

permit_fees.notes: The fee schedule is labeled Valuation Data Updated, effective 9/18/2025. The same schedule lists a Building Safety re-inspection fee of $75 (plus 24 hour delay), a $50 permit extension (up to 180 days), and an expedited permit review fee of two times the plan review fee for the associated permit type. The schedule does not say whether expedited review is offered for the flat-fee solar permit. The Town's sales tax page says that, effective Oct. 1, 2007, the Town's construction sales tax rate became 4.25 percent, and that total rates consist of city, county and state percentages. The page does not say how this tax applies to a solar installation. For questions about permit fees, the Town lists Kimberly Pippin at 480-358-3086.

value.name: SRP Demand Management System (DMS) rebate
value.description: SRP's residential program requirements say SRP is offering SRP customers a $250 rebate with the purchase of an approved Demand Management System (DMS). The rebate is limited to one per household. SRP says it may discontinue, suspend or modify the program at any time by posting a notice on its website.
value.eligibility: The DMS must be installed as part of a system installed by one of SRP's Preferred Solar Installers. The rebate must be requested with the SRP Program Application.

rebates.notes: The Town's solar page describes no Town rebate for solar PV.
